steps: Here a mixed ticket lands: the customer was charged twice, and the app crashes. Billing and technical, in one ticket.
A single agent handles both, and loses track. The crash is fixed, but was there a refund? It lost the thread.
So you refactor. An orchestrator decomposes the ticket into separable sub-tasks: the refund goes to billing, the crash goes to tech.
It delegates in parallel. Each specialist gets its own prompt, tools and model, in its own isolated context.
Each runs separately, and only final results return to the orchestrator: refund issued from billing, and root cause found from tech.
Now the orchestrator merges both results into one reply to the customer. Nothing is dropped this time, and the ticket is resolved.
Finally, a caution. Multi-agent adds calls and hand-offs, so a one-file fix stays single-agent. Split only when the work is separable, overflows context, or can run in parallel.
